- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent highs and underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecasts are often too optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term volatility.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, often underestimating sharp declines.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to overreaction to short-term spikes.
- Model underestimates true volatility in the final 10–15 days, especially when prices are trending downward.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp transitions, underestimating sudden drops or spikes in the last 5–10 days.
